predicted: Section 11's remaining scope limit: every result in Paper C is ONE-SHOT coefficient averaging, and section 6's recommendation -- shrink toward local by a locally chosen weight -- is established only for that setting. A reviewer will ask whether it survives iterative federated averaging, which is strictly more capable and is the standard baseline. MERGE_MODE=fedavg swaps the merged model at the SCORING boundary (30 rounds, 5 local epochs), leaving every policy definition untouched, so any difference is the merge rule and not a changed comparison. These are the five pools where the recommendation is most at risk: the three where merging HARMS (mimic4_sites, acs_span_traveltime, acs_full_income) and two where it clearly helps (eicu_sites, lendingclub). PREDICTION: blend still beats every binary policy on all five, and remains non-negative against never_merge, so section 6's recommendation carries over and section 11's scope limit can be narrowed rather than kept. A 1-seed probe on mimic4_sites already gives blend 37.5% of the lambda-oracle under FedAvg. WHAT WOULD MATTER: if a binary policy beats blend under iterative merging on any harmful pool, the recommendation is specific to one-shot merging and section 6 must SAY so rather than generalise. That is the honest outcome to look for, because iterative merging produces a stronger merged model and a stronger merged model is exactly the condition under which shrinking toward local should stop paying. blend_cw is reported as nan under this mode by design -- it needs the merged model's per-coordinate parameters, which FedAvg does not expose, and faking them would put a meaningless number in the table.
